alignments.note: Imperative; the copular auxiliary *Be* is a rule 7/9 helper and rule 17 puts the head on the lexical predicate *patient*.
Inferential conjunction.
Anarthrous vocative; no supplied address word, so rule 89 does not arise.
Improper preposition rendered by a single English word, so rule 42's frame question does not arise.
Article surfaces as *the* (rule 19); rule 42's closing clause gives it a bare *the* because the adverb is itself rendered by a single English word.
Head noun of the ἕως phrase.
Genitive article carries the case preposition under rule 21; *of the* is one unit headed on *the*.
Noun stands alone, its determiner and case preposition having gone with the article.
Presentative particle.
Article to *the* (rule 19).
Recoverable token pair with its article under rule 26.

*for* is the English verb's own particle: rule 36 assigns such a preposition to a Greek preposition only where one is expressed, and ἐκδέχεται takes a bare accusative here, so *waiteth for* stays one unit headed on the verb.
Article to *the*; rule 58's supplied-determiner clause does not apply, an article being present to take it.
Attributive adjective, bare, the article having taken the determiner (rule 58).
Head noun of the object phrase.
Genitive article with case preposition under rule 21, headed on *the*.
Noun alone.
Circumstantial participle rendered periphrastically; rule 17 heads on the lexical predicate *patient*, not the supplied copula, as s001 does for the same lexeme (rule 24).
Expressed preposition realized by *over* (rule 36).

Pronoun object of ἐπί; the ASV spreads the phrase over two words, so rules 35/45 do not arise (rule 94). Variant SBLGNT.JAS.5.7.v004 is underdetermined with the base among the permitted readings, so no rule 97 question arises.
Second ἕως, rendered by a single word as the first was (rule 24).

Subjunctive with its supplied English subject pronoun as a rule 9 helper, headed on the lexical verb. Variant SBLGNT.JAS.5.7.v005 is underdetermined with the base permitted, so rule 12 leaves it alone.

The Greek is anarthrous here, and the adjective is substantival, so under rule 58's substantival clause the adjective is the nominal word and takes the supplied determiner itself, exactly as νεκρῶν → *the dead* does.
Expressed conjunction, aligned in the ordinary way (rules 88, 98 untouched).

Second substantival adjective; the supplied generic noun *rain* completes the coordinated pair and is placed on the adjective it stands next to, rule 17 keeping the head on the adjective as it does for ταῦτα → *these things*. GEN.6.16 is the same construction and settles the placement: `תַּחְתִּיִּם` *with lower*, `שְׁנִיִּם` *second*, `שְׁלִשִׁים` *third stories* gives the frame word written once before the series to the first conjunct and the generic noun written once after it to the last, each unit `aligned` and headed on its adjective. Sharing *rain* across both adjectives is not a competing reading but an unrepresentable one: no target token in the finished corpus belongs to two units, so rule 30's shared target means one multi-source unit for one indivisible English word, and rule 2 forbids merging `πρόϊμον` with `ὄψιμον` while *early* and *latter* stay separately meaningful. Nothing is conceded: about forty corpus units fold a supplied generic noun onto an adjective, all `aligned` and all headed on the adjective, and JOL.2.23 `מַלְקוֹשׁ` → *the latter rain* heads on *latter* independently.

review_notes: Resubmission: the previous return was rejected only for carrying the wrong `ref`. The ref is JAS.5.7 and the alignment is returned unchanged, having been reviewed again against the contract and found correct.
Every s### and t### is partitioned exactly once; no unrepresented or added units were needed.
*for* at t015 is treated as the English phrasal verb's own particle rather than a realization of any Greek preposition, since ἐκδέχεται governs a bare accusative (rule 36's limiting clause).
The two supplied-determiner questions divide: t016 goes to the expressed article s013 under rules 19/58, while t029 goes to the substantival adjective s023 because no article stands in that phrase.
The supplied noun *rain* is treated as the coordinated adjectives' generic completion and attached to s025; the competing readings are named in that unit's note.
Both ἕως units are rendered by a single English word, so rule 42's frame question and rule 101's trailing-preposition question do not arise, and s005 takes a bare *the*.
